correctness.rationale: The final theorem exhausts finite-rank, finite-kernel, and infinite-rank/infinite-kernel partial isometries on separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert H, subdividing the last case by cokernel. Compact finite-rank W and finite-kernel W are absolutely norm attaining (finite dimensional spheres or intersection of every infinite-dimensional subspace with initial space). For noncompact S in the AN norm closure, inspected Ramesh–Sequeira Thm 3.7/Cor 3.8 supply |S|=alpha I+compact with alpha>0 and finite kernel. Kernel and initial-space orthonormal sequences force ||W−S||≥max(alpha,|1−alpha|)≥1/2; compact S yields ≥1. When both kernel and cokernel infinite, choose unitary extending W and use S=U/2 to attain 1/2. For finite cokernel, ||W−S||<1 gives an invertible compression P_R S|_M; the graph of −(P_R S|_M)^{-1}P_R S|_N maps into finite-dimensional R^perp, forcing infinite ker S, contradiction for noncompact S. Zero achieves 1. The projection/coisometry same-modulus example correctly distinguishes 1/2 and 1. No finite truncation is substituted for proof; external structural theorem verified at its primary source.
